subject: B
topic: Rapid mixed revision & weak-area drill — GK India

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Poona Pact' of 1932 was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and which leader regarding the representation of the depressed classes?
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed between Gandhi and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, replacing separate electorates with reserved seats for the depressed classes. Nehru, Malaviya and Bose were prominent leaders but not the signatories of this specific pact, so Ambedkar is the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Indian scientist is known as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'?
questions.explanation: Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme for founding ISRO. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam led missile development, Satish Dhawan and K. Sivan were later ISRO chairmen, so none of them holds this founding title except Sarabhai.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about world capitals:

(i) The capital of Australia is Canberra.
(ii) The capital of Canada is Ottawa.
(iii) The capital of the United States is New York.
(iv) The capital of Japan is Tokyo.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Canberra is Australia's capital (i), Ottawa is Canada's (ii), and Tokyo is Japan's (iv). Statement (iii) is false because the capital of the United States is Washington, D.C., not New York, so any option containing (iii) is eliminated, leaving '(i), (ii) and (iv)'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Kaziranga National Park', known for the one-horned rhinoceros, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the great one-horned rhinoceros, is in Assam. West Bengal has the Sundarbans, Odisha has Similipal, and Bihar has Valmiki, so none of them hosts Kaziranga, which lies in Assam along the Brahmaputra.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Ramsar Wetland Sites located in India?

(i) Chilika Lake
(ii) Loktak Lake
(iii) Sambhar Lake
(iv) Mount Abu

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Chilika, Loktak and Sambhar lakes are recognised Ramsar wetland sites. Mount Abu is a hill station in Rajasthan, not a wetland, so any combination containing (iv) is wrong, leaving '(i), (ii) and (iii)' as the correct set of Ramsar sites.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Battle of Buxar' (1764), which strengthened British control over Bengal, was fought against the combined forces of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh and which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: At Buxar, the British defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal (19th century), Aurangzeb died in 1707, and Farrukhsiyar ruled earlier, so Shah Alam II is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the largest state of India by geographical area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest Indian state by area. Madhya Pradesh is the second largest, while Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh are smaller in area, so none of them is the biggest, making Rajasthan the correct answer for the largest state by geographical size.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Tropic of Cancer divides India into roughly two climatic halves.
Reason (R): The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of the country, separating the tropical south from the subtropical north.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer splits India into two climatic halves (A) precisely because it runs through the middle, separating the tropical south from the subtropical north (R), so R correctly explains A. The options denying either statement are wrong since both are true, and its central passage is exactly why the climatic division occurs.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Khelo India' programme launched by the Government of India is aimed at promoting:
questions.explanation: Khelo India aims to revive a sporting culture and nurture talent at the grassroots. Digital literacy is targeted by programmes like PMGDISHA, rural electrification by schemes like Saubhagya, and organic farming by other missions, so promoting sports is the correct objective of Khelo India.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Radcliffe Line' forms the boundary between India and which country?
questions.explanation: The Radcliffe Line, drawn in 1947, demarcates the India–Pakistan (and India–Bangladesh) border. The India–China border is the McMahon Line/LAC, the India–Nepal border is defined by treaty, and India–Myanmar has its own boundary, so the Radcliffe Line refers to the Pakistan border.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following classical dance forms with the states they originated in:

Column I:
(a) Bharatanatyam
(b) Kathakali
(c) Odissi
(d) Kuchipudi

Column II:
(i) Kerala
(ii) Tamil Nadu
(iii) Andhra Pradesh
(iv) Odisha

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Kathakali from Kerala, Odissi from Odisha, and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh. The other options swap pairs, such as placing Bharatanatyam in Kerala or Odissi in Tamil Nadu, which are incorrect, so the first mapping is right.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the first Indian woman to serve as President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President of the Congress in 1925. Annie Besant was the first woman president (1917) but was of British-Irish origin; Indira Gandhi and Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit held other posts, so Sarojini Naidu is the first Indian woman to head the Congress.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Jog Falls', one of the highest waterfalls in India, is formed by which river?
questions.explanation: Jog Falls in Karnataka is formed by the Sharavati river. The Kaveri forms the Shivanasamudra Falls, the Godavari has other falls, and the Tungabhadra is a tributary of the Krishna, so none of them creates Jog Falls, which is on the Sharavati.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Constitutional Amendment is known for adding the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. The 44th Amendment reversed some emergency-era changes, the 1st Amendment dealt with land reforms and free speech, and the 73rd Amendment established Panchayati Raj, so the 42nd is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Simon Commission', which arrived in India in 1928, was boycotted mainly because:
options: It proposed the partition of India
It banned the Indian National Congress
questions.explanation: The Simon Commission was boycotted because all its members were British with no Indian representation, prompting the slogan 'Simon Go Back'. It did not propose partition, did not ban the Congress, and was not about land tax, so the absence of Indian members is the correct reason.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's major crops:

(i) Rice is a kharif crop.
(ii) Wheat is a rabi crop.
(iii) India is the largest producer of jute in the world.
(iv) Cotton grows best in the black soil of the Deccan.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Rice is a kharif crop (i), wheat a rabi crop (ii), India is the largest jute producer (iii), and cotton thrives in Deccan black soil (iv), so all four statements are correct. The combinations that omit any one are therefore incomplete, making the 'all four' option correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Bengal Famine' that caused massive loss of life occurred in which year?
questions.explanation: The Bengal Famine occurred in 1943 during the Second World War. 1857 was the year of the Revolt, 1919 saw the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, and 1905 was the partition of Bengal, so none of those is the famine year, which is 1943.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bengal' due to its historically destructive floods?
questions.explanation: The Damodar was called the 'Sorrow of Bengal' before the Damodar Valley Corporation controlled its floods. The Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar', while the Hooghly and Teesta are other rivers of the region without this specific epithet, so the Damodar is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Digital India' programme was launched by the Government of India primarily to:
options: Transform India into a digitally empowered society
questions.correctAnswer: Transform India into a digitally empowered society
questions.explanation: Digital India aims to make India a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy with better e-governance and connectivity. Free LPG is the Ujjwala scheme, rural roads are under PMGSY, and crop insurance is Fasal Bima, so digital empowerment is the correct objective.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The monsoon is very important for Indian agriculture.
Reason (R): A large part of Indian farming depends on rainfall as many areas lack assured irrigation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The monsoon is vital for Indian agriculture (A) precisely because much farming is rain-dependent as many regions lack assured irrigation (R), so R correctly explains A. The options denying either statement are wrong since both are true, and rain-dependence is exactly why the monsoon matters so much.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Nalanda University', an ancient centre of learning, was located in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: The ancient Nalanda University was in present-day Bihar. Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh have their own historical sites, but the famous Buddhist university of Nalanda was located in Bihar, so it is the correct state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are permanent members of the UN Security Council?

(i) United States
(ii) China
(iii) India
(iv) Russia

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The United States, China and Russia are permanent (veto-holding) members of the UN Security Council, along with the UK and France. India is a non-permanent member elected periodically, not a permanent one, so any combination containing (iii) is wrong, leaving '(i), (ii) and (iv)'.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chauri Chaura incident' of 1922, which led Gandhi to withdraw a major movement, took place in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: The Chauri Chaura incident, where a mob set fire to a police station, occurred in present-day Uttar Pradesh and led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement. Bihar, Gujarat and Maharashtra were not the site of this event, so Uttar Pradesh is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The currency of which country is the 'Dinar'?
questions.explanation: Kuwait uses the Dinar as its currency. Turkey uses the Lira, Iran the Rial, and Egypt the Egyptian Pound, so none of them uses the Dinar, making Kuwait the correct answer among the given countries.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Grand Trunk Road', one of Asia's oldest and longest roads, was significantly rebuilt and extended by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri rebuilt and extended the Grand Trunk Road in the 16th century, improving trade and administration. Akbar ruled later, Ashoka much earlier, and Krishnadevaraya was a southern king, so the road's major reconstruction is credited to Sher Shah Suri.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian awards with the fields in which they are given:

Column I:
(a) Bharat Ratna
(b) Param Vir Chakra
(c) Dronacharya Award
(d) Jnanpith Award

Column II:
(i) Highest wartime gallantry
(ii) Highest civilian honour
(iii) Literature
(iv) Excellence in sports coaching

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian honour, the Param Vir Chakra the highest wartime gallantry award, the Dronacharya Award is for excellence in sports coaching, and the Jnanpith Award is for literature. The other options swap pairs, such as making Bharat Ratna a gallantry award, which is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Western Ghats', a biodiversity hotspot, run parallel to which coast of India?
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats run parallel to the western coast along the Arabian Sea. The Eastern Ghats lie along the Bay of Bengal coast, the southern tip is where the two ranges meet, and the northern plains are far from the Ghats, so the western coast is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The book 'Gitanjali', which won the Nobel Prize, was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings) was written by Rabindranath Tagore and earned him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature. Bankim Chandra, Sarat Chandra and Kazi Nazrul Islam were other notable Bengali writers but did not author 'Gitanjali', so Tagore is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the food-grain production (in million tonnes) of a country over four years:

2021 → 250
2022 → 275
2023 → 300
2024 → 315

What was the total increase in production from 2021 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Increase = 315 − 250 = 65 million tonnes. '50' and '40' are only partial year-to-year increases, and '70' overstates the total, so the correct overall increase from 2021 to 2024 is 65 million tonnes.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which committee's recommendations led to the establishment of the Panchayati Raj system in India?
questions.explanation: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj system. The Sarkaria Commission dealt with Centre-State relations, the Kothari Commission with education, and the Swaran Singh Committee with Fundamental Duties, so none of them founded Panchayati Raj except the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Sundarbans support a rich variety of wildlife including the Royal Bengal Tiger.
Reason (R): The Sundarbans form the world's largest mangrove forest, providing a unique tidal habitat.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans support rich wildlife like the Royal Bengal Tiger (A) precisely because they form the world's largest mangrove forest with a unique tidal habitat (R), so R correctly explains A. The options denying either statement are wrong since both are true, and the mangrove habitat is exactly why such wildlife thrives there.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India' for integrating the princely states after independence?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India' for uniting over 500 princely states into the Indian Union. Nehru was the first PM, Shastri a later PM, and Rajendra Prasad the first President, so none of them holds this title except Patel.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Chandrayaan-3' mission of ISRO successfully achieved which milestone?
options: A soft landing near the Moon's south pole
questions.correctAnswer: A soft landing near the Moon's south pole
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to soft-land near the Moon's south polar region. It was not a crewed mission, did not land on Mars, and did not fly by Jupiter, so the soft landing near the lunar south pole is the correct achievement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are members of the 'BRICS' grouping (original five members)?

(i) Brazil
(ii) Russia
(iii) India
(iv) Japan

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Brazil, Russia and India are among the original BRICS members (with China and South Africa). Japan is not a BRICS member, so any combination containing (iv) is wrong, leaving '(i), (ii) and (iii)' as the correct set of listed members.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Wular Lake', one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, and the 'Dal Lake' are situated in which region of India?
questions.explanation: Both the Wular and Dal lakes are in the Kashmir Valley of Jammu and Kashmir. Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Sikkim have other lakes, but these two famous lakes belong to J&K, so it is the correct region.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Mughal emperor built the 'Taj Mahal' in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, Jahangir is linked to gardens in Kashmir, and Humayun's own tomb was built by his widow, so Shah Jahan is the correct builder of the Taj Mahal.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'FIFA World Cup' is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The FIFA World Cup is the premier international football tournament. Cricket has the ICC World Cup, hockey has its own World Cup, and tennis has Grand Slam tournaments, so the FIFA World Cup specifically belongs to football.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Konkan Railway', a major engineering achievement, connects which two coastal regions?
options: Maharashtra and Karnataka/Goa along the west coast
questions.correctAnswer: Maharashtra and Karnataka/Goa along the west coast
questions.explanation: The Konkan Railway runs along the western coast, linking Maharashtra with Goa and Karnataka through difficult terrain. It does not connect Tamil Nadu–Kerala, Odisha–West Bengal, or Gujarat–Rajasthan, so the Maharashtra–Goa–Karnataka corridor is the correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which fundamental right is described as the 'heart and soul' of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because it allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court to enforce their rights. The Rights to Equality, Freedom and against Exploitation are important but were not given this description, so the first option is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Ozone Day' is observed internationally on which date to raise awareness about protecting the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed on 16 September. 5 June is World Environment Day, 22 April is Earth Day, and 21 June is International Yoga Day, so none of those is Ozone Day, which falls on 16 September.
